messages:
zara: quick micro-decision for billing UI—should the spend legend show absolute $ values or relative % by default? charts get messy when both are shown. figma comps: https://www.figma.com/file/unique/billing-legend-choices

leo: i vote absolute by default. when folks are scanning bills they want exactness. percent can be a hover tooltip or secondary column.

paul: agree on default absolute. but for org-level views where totals are huge, % helps compare tiny line items. suggestion: default absolute + a toggle on the legend header to switch to % mode. small toggle, remembered per-user.

nina: accessibility: toggles must have aria-label like "Toggle legend unit: dollars or percent" and expose current state with aria-pressed. also ensure the percent column is included in table order for screen readers if visible.

sana: contrast note: the legend keys (small colored badges) are failing contrast on dark theme for low-spend items. increase badge border or use a patterned fill for low-contrast colors. pattern is heavier work; border plus high-contrast text might suffice.

keith: engineering feasibility: adding a secondary column for percent is cheap. persisting user preference per account (or per browser?)—we should do per-user server-side so it's consistent across devices. adds a simple user preference in backend.

zara: product thought: what about a condensed mode for legends on narrow widths—show icons + abbreviated labels and link to full legend drawer. avoids overflow.

leo: condensed + drawer seems good. but make sure drawer is keyboard accessible and SR-friendly. role=dialog with aria-labelledby.

paul: on invoices: some users expect the invoice PDF to match the visible legend unit (dollars vs percent). PDFs should default to absolute dollars but include a size note if percent-only chosen. maybe include a small footnote: "Percent column omitted from PDF; values in UI were percentages."

nina: PDFs & accessibility: make sure tables in PDFs have proper semantic table headers. the earlier PDFs lost header rows for screen readers in NVDA. filing a ticket: https://jira.redwood/ISSUE-INV123

sana: suggestion: in the UI when user switches legend unit to percent, show a tiny helper text: "Export will default to dollars; use Export options to include percent." keeps expectation clear.

keith: export options modal is doable. add checkbox: "Include percent column (may inflate file size)". default off. modal will remember last choice per user.

zara: another small concern: org vs project scope—when switching scope, the legend items reorder (top spenders first). this causes layout shift and can be disorienting. maybe keep stable ordering with a small chevron to sort by spend.

leo: stable ordering makes sense. default to model name alphabetical for consistent reading order, with a sort control to switch to "Sort by spend". keep a tooltip explaining current order.

paul: for mobile, show only top 2 legend rows inline, and a "View all" link that opens a full-screen drawer. ensure the drawer has a clear close control in top-right and returns focus to trigger on close.

nina: a11y checklist for drawer: 1) role=dialog, 2) aria-modal=true, 3) focus trap + return, 4) escape closes, 5) close button labeled "Close legend".

sana: tiny copy tweak for mobile "View all spend items" -> prefer "View full legend" (shorter and clearer).

designbot: uploaded a new mock with fixed-order legend + export modal: https://assets.redwood/screencap/legend-export-modal-v1.png

keith: implementation notes: 1) add userPref legend_unit (dollars|percent), 2) persist per-user, 3) add server flag export_include_percent default false, 4) create LegendDrawer component with accessibility props. ETA PR in 4 days.

zara: can someone own writing the small bits of copy for export modal & helper text? i'll take a pass and post in figma.

leo: i'll QA the PDF output once keith finishes. will test with large org dataset to ensure header rows survive.

paul: action recap: zara -> copy for export modal; keith -> backend pref + LegendDrawer + export modal; leo -> PDF QA; nina/sana -> accessibility review; designbot -> push updated tokens for badge borders. feature flagged: `legend_units_and_export_v1`.

keith: one more tech note: when switching between dollars and percent, animate numeric transitions to avoid jarring jumps but keep reduced-motion respected. use requestAnimationFrame + pref reduced motion check.

zara: great. i'll draft the copy and link it here by EOD. thanks all :sparkles:
